topics.label: Tasmania · florfenicol
topics.status: Not re-authorised yet — 2 applications before the APVMA, decision on the industry's permit expected late November

timeline.t: APVMA grants an emergency use permit (no. 96499) for the antibiotic florfenicol against the summer disease outbreak (10–20 mg/kg of fish a day for 10 days, no re-treatment).
Tasmanian regulator statement: traces found in wild fish (up to 0.06 mg/kg, as far as 10.6 km from the pens); the APVMA suspends the permit later in February.
APVMA revokes the permit over an 'unacceptable risk of residue exposure to non-target species'.
Salmon Tasmania: 5.4 t used against the outbreak that killed about 9,000 t of salmon; the industry applies again.
Abbey Labs applies for a 'minor use' permit with a higher dose and treatment regime, extended from the south-east to the eastern biosecurity zone; dose rates not disclosed.

Salmon Tasmania's emergency application (same dose as the revoked permit; D'Entrecasteaux Channel and Storm Bay only, on vet advice) comes with wild-fishery closures of up to six weeks and compensation; rock lobster fishers refuse it. APVMA decision expected later this month.
